variants.label: top block relocated into the free band, then squeezed
variants.architecture: The five small rooms plus I form a linear chain I->A->B->C->D->E->BIG1 whose pipes are all internal except ONE (E's bottom port into BIG1's top port at column 17). So the block is translated rigidly (+62 rows, +69 cols) into the 57x261 band that the plotter_03 trim freed beside the three big rooms, and only that single connection is re-drawn. Rows 59-61 are blocked at columns 46-69, so the new route climbs a corridor at column 82, runs west along row 1 and comes back down column 17. Straight runs are drawn with segment glyphs ('|','-') rather than arrowheads so alexey_squeeze can still see through them; it then removed 59 rows and 25 columns.
variants.verdict: TEAM BEST for plotter: 16,905,772,730 -> 9,367,793,668 (1.80x), and 8.1x against the 75.8B this line started from. The long re-route was expected to cost ticks and instead SAVED them (114,065 -> 88,146), because the squeeze that followed shortened every pipe crossing the 59 deleted rows, not just this one.

variants.label: every room shrunk to its content (empty edge rows/columns dropped)
variants.architecture: Per-room edge trim via src/littleman/alexey_trimrooms.py: each wall moves inward past that room's own empty edge rows/columns, and any pipe attached to the wall is extended to reach the new one. Seven rooms shrank -- five lost 8 empty left columns each, one lost 62, one lost 2 bottom rows; 104 edge lines in all. The LM-75 display is skipped, its blank interior being the drawing surface.
variants.verdict: NOT AN IMPROVEMENT on its own -- 16,907,343,915 against plotter_02's 16,905,772,730, 0.01% worse because the pipe extensions cost 7 ticks. A narrower room still sits in the same bounding box. Kept because it is the base for the move step: after the trim, rows 62-322 have columns 81-137 entirely free (57 wide by 261 tall), and the six trimmed rooms are now at most 34 wide and total 52 rows. Relocating them there would free rows 5-58 and 330-339, taking the height from 385 to about 320 -- footprint ~102,400, about 1.45x. Needs roughly twelve pipes re-routed.

variants.label: mechanical squeeze of empty rows/columns
variants.architecture: Whole-program squeeze via src/littleman/alexey_squeeze.py (full): every row made only of ' ' and '|', and every column made only of ' ' and '-', is deleted. No room re-laid, no pipe re-routed. Shortens each room interior and each vertical pipe it crosses by one cell; the walk is identical apart from being shorter, which is why ticks fall too.
variants.verdict: TEAM BEST for plotter: 75,794,498,065 -> 16,905,772,730 (4.48x). Most of the gain on the large programs is ticks, not area -- the surviving pipes got shorter.

note: Alexey research line for plotter. plotter_04 is the current best at 9,367,793,668 -- 8.1x better than the 75,794,498,065 this line started from. Chain: plotter_02 (mechanical squeeze) -> plotter_03 (rooms trimmed to content, a deliberate no-op) -> plotter_04 (top block relocated into the band the trim freed).
